title: ERROR_END_OF_MEDIA (error 1100, 0x8007044C)
summary: 0x8007044C is a Windows system error: "The physical end of the tape has been reached". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: ERROR_END_OF_MEDIA (error 1100, 0x8007044C) is a Windows system error code with the official message "The physical end of the tape has been reached". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: ERROR_FILEMARK_DETECTED (error 1101, 0x8007044D)
summary: 0x8007044D means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("A tape access reached a filemark"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_FILEMARK_DETECTED (error 1101, 0x8007044D) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_SERIAL_NO_DEVICE (error 1118, 0x8007045E)
summary: 0x8007045E means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: ERROR_SERIAL_NO_DEVICE (error 1118, 0x8007045E) is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: ERROR_FLOPPY_ID_MARK_NOT_FOUND (error 1122, 0x80070462)
summary: 0x80070462 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("No ID address mark was found on the floppy disk"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_FLOPPY_ID_MARK_NOT_FOUND (error 1122, 0x80070462) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_FLOPPY_UNKNOWN_ERROR (error 1124, 0x80070464)
summary: 0x80070464 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: ERROR_FLOPPY_UNKNOWN_ERROR (error 1124, 0x80070464) is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

title: ERROR_EOM_OVERFLOW (error 1129, 0x80070469)
summary: 0x80070469 is a Windows system error: "Physical end of tape encountered". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: ERROR_EOM_OVERFLOW (error 1129, 0x80070469) is a Windows system error code with the official message "Physical end of tape encountered". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: ERROR_OLD_WIN_VERSION (error 1150, 0x8007047E)
summary: 0x8007047E points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: ERROR_OLD_WIN_VERSION (error 1150, 0x8007047E) points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: ERROR_INVALID_DLL (error 1154, 0x80070482)
summary: 0x80070482 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("One of the library files needed to run this application is damaged"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_INVALID_DLL (error 1154, 0x80070482) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_DDE_FAIL (error 1156, 0x80070484)

The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software

title: ERROR_UNABLE_TO_REMOVE_REPLACED (error 1175, 0x80070497)
summary: 0x80070497 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("Unable to remove the file to be replaced"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_UNABLE_TO_REMOVE_REPLACED (error 1175, 0x80070497) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

summary: 0x8007049A slows the PC down. Find the process responsible in Task Manager, then work through the fixes below.
meaning: ERROR_JOURNAL_DELETE_IN_PROGRESS (error 1178, 0x8007049A) is a performance problem rather than a crash: something is using more CPU, disk, memory or time than it should. Finding the process responsible is usually the whole battle.
commonCauses: Too many apps launching at startup
A background update, indexing or antivirus scan
Malware or unwanted software
A nearly full or failing drive
Outdated drivers

fixes.title: Find the process using the resources
fixes.detail: Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc), go to Processes and sort by CPU, Memory or Disk. Note the top process before changing anything.

fixes.title: Trim startup apps
fixes.detail: Task Manager > Startup apps: disable anything you do not need at sign-in.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep 15-20% of the system drive free
Uninstall software you no longer use
Avoid running multiple antivirus products

fixes.title: Trim startup apps

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

title: ERROR_POTENTIAL_FILE_FOUND (error 1180, 0x8007049C)
summary: 0x8007049C means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("A file was found, but it may not be the correct file"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_POTENTIAL_FILE_FOUND (error 1180, 0x8007049C) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.

Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.

title: ERROR_DEVICE_ALREADY_REMEMBERED (error 1202, 0x800704B2)
summary: 0x800704B2 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: ERROR_DEVICE_ALREADY_REMEMBERED (error 1202, 0x800704B2) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: ERROR_INVALID_NETNAME (error 1214, 0x800704BE)
summary: 0x800704BE means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: ERROR_INVALID_NETNAME (error 1214, 0x800704BE) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: ERROR_CANCELLED (error 1223, 0x800704C7)
summary: 0x800704C7 (ERROR_CANCELLED) is a Windows system error: "The operation was canceled by the user". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: ERROR_CANCELLED (error 1223, 0x800704C7) is a Windows system error code with the official message "The operation was canceled by the user". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed. Technically, 0x800704C7 is an HRESULT that wraps Win32 error 1223 (ERROR_CANCELLED).
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: ERROR_USER_MAPPED_FILE (error 1224, 0x800704C8)
summary: 0x800704C8 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("The requested operation cannot be performed on a file with a user-mapped section open"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_USER_MAPPED_FILE (error 1224, 0x800704C8) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

meaning: ERROR_CONNECTION_ABORTED (error 1236, 0x800704D4) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: ERROR_RETRY (error 1237, 0x800704D5)
summary: 0x800704D5 is a Windows system error: "The operation could not be completed. A retry should be performed". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: ERROR_RETRY (error 1237, 0x800704D5) is a Windows system error code with the official message "The operation could not be completed. A retry should be performed". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates

title: ERROR_BAD_USER_PROFILE (error 1253, 0x800704E5)

meaning: ERROR_BAD_USER_PROFILE (error 1253, 0x800704E5) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.

Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_HOST_DOWN (error 1256, 0x800704E8)
summary: 0x800704E8 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: ERROR_HOST_DOWN (error 1256, 0x800704E8) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.

Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: ERROR_ACCESS_DISABLED_BY_POLICY (error 1260, 0x800704EC)
summary: 0x800704EC points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: ERROR_ACCESS_DISABLED_BY_POLICY (error 1260, 0x800704EC) points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: ERROR_SYNC_FOREGROUND_REFRESH_REQUIRED (error 1274, 0x800704FA)
summary: 0x800704FA points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: ERROR_SYNC_FOREGROUND_REFRESH_REQUIRED (error 1274, 0x800704FA) points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: ERROR_DRIVER_BLOCKED (error 1275, 0x800704FB)
summary: 0x800704FB means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: ERROR_DRIVER_BLOCKED (error 1275, 0x800704FB) is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: ERROR_ACCESS_DISABLED_WEBBLADE_TAMPER (error 1278, 0x800704FE)
summary: Windows activation failed with 0x800704FE. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.

A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

prevention: Link your digital license to your Microsoft account
Buy keys from Microsoft or authorized sellers
Keep a record of the product key and where it came from

title: ERROR_RECOVERY_FAILURE (error 1279, 0x800704FF)
summary: 0x800704FF appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: ERROR_RECOVERY_FAILURE (error 1279, 0x800704FF) appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

title: ERROR_INVALID_OWNER (error 1307, 0x8007051B)
summary: 0x8007051B means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("This security ID may not be assigned as the owner of this object"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: ERROR_INVALID_OWNER (error 1307, 0x8007051B) is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

title: ERROR_NO_IMPERSONATION_TOKEN (error 1309, 0x8007051D)
summary: 0x8007051D is a Windows system error: "An attempt has been made to operate on an impersonation token by a thread that is not currently impersonating a client". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: ERROR_NO_IMPERSONATION_TOKEN (error 1309, 0x8007051D) is a Windows system error code with the official message "An attempt has been made to operate on an impersonation token by a thread that is not currently impersonating a client". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

title: ERROR_WRONG_PASSWORD (error 1323, 0x8007052B)
summary: Windows Update reported 0x8007052B ("Unable to update the password. The value provided as the current password is incorrect") and the update could not finish. Clearing the update cache and repairing system components fixes most cases.
meaning: ERROR_WRONG_PASSWORD (error 1323, 0x8007052B) is a result code returned while Windows Update was downloading, preparing or installing an update. Its underlying message is: "Unable to update the password. The value provided as the current password is incorrect". The update itself is rarely broken; the usual problem is on the PC: a corrupted download cache, stopped update services, too little free space, damaged system components or something blocking the connection to Microsoft's servers.
commonCauses: A corrupted or half-finished download in the SoftwareDistribution cache
Windows Update, BITS or Cryptographic services stopped or disabled
Too little free space on the system drive
Corrupted component store or system files
A VPN, proxy, firewall or third-party antivirus interfering with the download

fixes.title: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and click Run next to Windows Update. On Windows 10 it is under Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot. Restart and try again.

fixes.title: Free up disk space
fixes.detail: Make sure the system drive has at least 20 GB free. Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files lets you remove old update files and other clutter safely.

fixes.title: Reset the update download cache
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `net stop wuauserv`, `net stop bits` and `net stop cryptsvc`. Rename the cache with `ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old`, then start the services again with `net start cryptsvc`, `net start bits` and `net start wuauserv`.
fixes.riskNote: Renaming the folder clears your local update history view. Installed updates are not affected.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Install the update manually
fixes.detail: Note the KB number shown in Settings > Windows Update, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com), download the package for your Windows version and architecture, and run it.

fixes.title: Run an in-place repair install as a last resort
fixes.detail: Download the Windows installation media from Microsoft, run setup.exe from inside Windows and choose to keep personal files and apps. It replaces every system file without wiping your data.
fixes.riskNote: Back up your important files before starting, and keep the PC plugged in until setup completes.

prevention: Keep at least 20 GB free on the system drive
Do not shut down while "Working on updates" is on screen
Pause VPNs and third-party firewalls while large updates download
Run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth` now and then to catch component damage early

title: ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (error 1344, 0x80070540)
summary: Windows Update reported 0x80070540 ("No more memory is available for security information updates") and the update could not finish. Clearing the update cache and repairing system components fixes most cases.
meaning: ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (error 1344, 0x80070540) is a result code returned while Windows Update was downloading, preparing or installing an update. Its underlying message is: "No more memory is available for security information updates". The update itself is rarely broken; the usual problem is on the PC: a corrupted download cache, stopped update services, too little free space, damaged system components or something blocking the connection to Microsoft's servers.
commonCauses: A corrupted or half-finished download in the SoftwareDistribution cache
Windows Update, BITS or Cryptographic services stopped or disabled
Too little free space on the system drive
Corrupted component store or system files
A VPN, proxy, firewall or third-party antivirus interfering with the download

fixes.title: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and click Run next to Windows Update. On Windows 10 it is under Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot. Restart and try again.

fixes.title: Free up disk space
fixes.detail: Make sure the system drive has at least 20 GB free. Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files lets you remove old update files and other clutter safely.

fixes.title: Reset the update download cache
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `net stop wuauserv`, `net stop bits` and `net stop cryptsvc`. Rename the cache with `ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old`, then start the services again with `net start cryptsvc`, `net start bits` and `net start wuauserv`.
fixes.riskNote: Renaming the folder clears your local update history view. Installed updates are not affected.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Install the update manually
fixes.detail: Note the KB number shown in Settings > Windows Update, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com), download the package for your Windows version and architecture, and run it.

fixes.title: Run an in-place repair install as a last resort
fixes.detail: Download the Windows installation media from Microsoft, run setup.exe from inside Windows and choose to keep personal files and apps. It replaces every system file without wiping your data.
fixes.riskNote: Back up your important files before starting, and keep the PC plugged in until setup completes.

prevention: Keep at least 20 GB free on the system drive
Do not shut down while "Working on updates" is on screen
Pause VPNs and third-party firewalls while large updates download
Run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth` now and then to catch component damage early

title: ERROR_INTERNAL_DB_CORRUPTION (error 1358, 0x8007054E)
summary: 0x8007054E means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("Unable to complete the requested operation because of either a catastrophic media failure or a data structure corruption on the disk"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_INTERNAL_DB_CORRUPTION (error 1358, 0x8007054E) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.

summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0x80070565 and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.

A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep the clock synced automatically

Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_INVALID_SPI_VALUE (error 1439, 0x8007059F)
summary: 0x8007059F points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: ERROR_INVALID_SPI_VALUE (error 1439, 0x8007059F) points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: ERROR_PAGEFILE_QUOTA (error 1454, 0x800705AE)
summary: 0x800705AE means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("Insufficient quota to complete the requested service"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_PAGEFILE_QUOTA (error 1454, 0x800705AE) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_NO_NVRAM_RESOURCES (error 1470, 0x800705BE)
summary: 0x800705BE appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: ERROR_NO_NVRAM_RESOURCES (error 1470, 0x800705BE) appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed

title: ERROR_BAD_CONFIGURATION (error 1610, 0x8007064A)
summary: 0x8007064A means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("The configuration data for this product is corrupt. Contact your support personnel"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_BAD_CONFIGURATION (error 1610, 0x8007064A) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: ERROR_INSTALL_LOG_FAILURE (error 1622, 0x80070656)
summary: 0x80070656 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("Error opening installation log file. Verify that the specified log file location exists and that you can write to it"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: ERROR_INSTALL_LOG_FAILURE (error 1622, 0x80070656) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

meaning: ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE (error 1630, 0x8007065E) is a Windows system error code with the official message "Data of this type is not supported". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: ERROR_INSTALL_TEMP_UNWRITABLE (error 1632, 0x80070660)
summary: 0x80070660 means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("The Temp folder is on a drive that is full or is inaccessible. Free up space on the drive or verify that you have write permission on the Temp folder"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: ERROR_INSTALL_TEMP_UNWRITABLE (error 1632, 0x80070660) is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Check Windows Security status
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Run one antivirus product at a time
Use a standard account for daily work
Keep Windows Security definitions up to date
