title: Error 0xC00002DA
summary: 0xC00002DA points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC00002DA points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

title: Error 0xC00002E1
summary: 0xC00002E1 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_DS_CANT_START The directory service cannot start". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC00002E1 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_DS_CANT_START The directory service cannot start". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC00002E2
summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0xC00002E2 and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC00002E2 comes from the Microsoft Store or the app installer service. It means the Store could not download, license or install an app package. The cause is usually local: a stale Store cache, the wrong date and time, a sign-in problem or a stopped service.
commonCauses: A corrupted Microsoft Store cache
Incorrect date, time or region settings
A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep the clock synced automatically
Install Windows updates, since they include Store framework fixes
Avoid blocking Microsoft endpoints in firewall or hosts files

title: Error 0xC00002E3
summary: 0xC00002E3 means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("STATUS_SAM_INIT_FAILURE The Security Accounts Manager initialization failed because of the following error: %hs Error Status: 0x%x. Click OK to shut down this system and restart in Safe Mode. Check the event log for more detailed information"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: Error 0xC00002E3 is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Check Windows Security status
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Run one antivirus product at a time
Use a standard account for daily work
Keep Windows Security definitions up to date

title: Error 0xC00002EA
summary: 0xC00002EA means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_CANNOT_MAKE The directory or file cannot be created"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC00002EA relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0000304
summary: 0xC0000304 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_MFT_TOO_FRAGMENTED The master file table on the volume is too fragmented to complete this operation"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0000304 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0000309
summary: 0xC0000309 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0000309 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0000352 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0000359
summary: 0xC0000359 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_WIN_32 The specified image file did not have the correct format; it appears to be a 32-bit Windows image"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0000359 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC000035C
summary: 0xC000035C means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC000035C is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC000035F
summary: 0xC000035F means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC000035F is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC0000366
summary: 0xC0000366 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0000366 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0000371
summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0xC0000371 and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC0000371 comes from the Microsoft Store or the app installer service. It means the Store could not download, license or install an app package. The cause is usually local: a stale Store cache, the wrong date and time, a sign-in problem or a stopped service.
commonCauses: A corrupted Microsoft Store cache
Incorrect date, time or region settings
A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep the clock synced automatically
Install Windows updates, since they include Store framework fixes
Avoid blocking Microsoft endpoints in firewall or hosts files

title: Error 0xC0000372

commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

title: Error 0xC0000374
summary: 0xC0000374 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION A heap has been corrupted"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0000374 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

summary: 0xC0000388 means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("STATUS_DOWNGRADE_DETECTED The system detected a possible attempt to compromise security. Ensure that you can contact the server that authenticated you"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: Error 0xC0000388 is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Check Windows Security status
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Run one antivirus product at a time
Use a standard account for daily work
Keep Windows Security definitions up to date

title: Error 0xC000038E
summary: 0xC000038E means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC000038E is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC0000410
summary: 0xC0000410 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0000410 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC0000413
summary: 0xC0000413 means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("STATUS_AUTHENTICATION_FIREWALL_FAILED Logon Failure: The machine you are logging onto is protected by an authentication firewall. The specified account is not allowed to authenticate to the machine"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: Error 0xC0000413 is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Check Windows Security status
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Run one antivirus product at a time
Use a standard account for daily work
Keep Windows Security definitions up to date

title: Error 0xC0000415
summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0xC0000415 and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC0000415 comes from the Microsoft Store or the app installer service. It means the Store could not download, license or install an app package. The cause is usually local: a stale Store cache, the wrong date and time, a sign-in problem or a stopped service.
commonCauses: A corrupted Microsoft Store cache
Incorrect date, time or region settings
A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep the clock synced automatically
Install Windows updates, since they include Store framework fixes
Avoid blocking Microsoft endpoints in firewall or hosts files

title: Error 0xC0000417
summary: 0xC0000417 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0000417 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC0000424
summary: 0xC0000424 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC0000424 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC0000453
summary: 0xC0000453 appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: Error 0xC0000453 appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

title: Error 0xC0000460
summary: 0xC0000460 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_NO_RANGES_PROCESSED No ranges for the specified operation were able to be processed". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC0000460 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_NO_RANGES_PROCESSED No ranges for the specified operation were able to be processed". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0000466
summary: 0xC0000466 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE The file server is temporarily unavailable"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0000466 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0000709
summary: 0xC0000709 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0000709 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC0000800

Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC000A012
summary: 0xC000A012 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC000A012 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC000A101
summary: 0xC000A101 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_HASH_NOT_PRESENT The hash requests is not present or not up to date with the current file contents"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC000A101 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

fixes.title: Scan for malware

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep 15-20% of the system drive free
Uninstall software you no longer use
Avoid running multiple antivirus products

title: Error 0xC0020008
summary: 0xC0020008 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0020008 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC0020019
summary: 0xC0020019 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0020019 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

meaning: Error 0xC002001B is a Windows system error code with the official message "RPC_NT_CALL_FAILED The RPC failed". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0020028
summary: 0xC0020028 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0020028 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC0020040
summary: 0xC0020040 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0020040 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

meaning: Error 0xC0020050 is a Windows system error code with the official message "RPC_NT_CALL_CANCELLED The RPC was canceled". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0020057
summary: 0xC0020057 means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("RPC_NT_SEC_PKG_ERROR A security package-specific error occurred"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: Error 0xC0020057 is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Check Windows Security status
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Run one antivirus product at a time
Use a standard account for daily work
Keep Windows Security definitions up to date

meaning: Error 0xC0030002 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
