title: Error 0xC0030004
summary: 0xC0030004 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0030004 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC0030005
summary: 0xC0030005 is a Windows system error: "RPC_NT_SS_CONTEXT_MISMATCH The context handle does not match any known context handles". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC0030005 is a Windows system error code with the official message "RPC_NT_SS_CONTEXT_MISMATCH The context handle does not match any known context handles". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

fixes.title: Find the process using the resources
fixes.detail: Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc), go to Processes and sort by CPU, Memory or Disk. Note the top process before changing anything.

fixes.title: Trim startup apps

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

prevention: Keep 15-20% of the system drive free

title: Error 0xC0040035
summary: Windows activation failed with 0xC0040035. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.
meaning: Error 0xC0040035 is an activation result. Windows could not confirm that this PC has a valid license, either because the key does not match the installed edition, the license is tied to different hardware, or the activation servers could not be reached.
commonCauses: A product key for a different edition (Home vs Pro)
A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

prevention: Link your digital license to your Microsoft account
Buy keys from Microsoft or authorized sellers
Keep a record of the product key and where it came from

title: Error 0xC00A0002
summary: 0xC00A0002 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0002 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers

title: Error 0xC00A0006
summary: 0xC00A0006 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_CTX_CLOSE_PENDING A close operation is pending on the terminal connection". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0006 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_CTX_CLOSE_PENDING A close operation is pending on the terminal connection". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC00A0008
summary: 0xC00A0008 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_CTX_MODEM_INF_NOT_FOUND The MODEM.INF file was not found"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0008 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC00A0010
summary: 0xC00A0010 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0010 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC00A0012
summary: Windows activation failed with 0xC00A0012. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0012 is an activation result. Windows could not confirm that this PC has a valid license, either because the key does not match the installed edition, the license is tied to different hardware, or the activation servers could not be reached.
commonCauses: A product key for a different edition (Home vs Pro)
A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

prevention: Link your digital license to your Microsoft account
Buy keys from Microsoft or authorized sellers
Keep a record of the product key and where it came from

summary: Windows activation failed with 0xC00A0014. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.

A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

title: Error 0xC00A0024
summary: 0xC00A0024 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0024 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC00A0030
summary: 0xC00A0030 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_CTX_SHADOW_INVALID The requested session cannot be controlled remotely. fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated

title: Error 0xC00A0033
summary: Windows activation failed with 0xC00A0033. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.
meaning: Error 0xC00A0033 is an activation result. Windows could not confirm that this PC has a valid license, either because the key does not match the installed edition, the license is tied to different hardware, or the activation servers could not be reached.
commonCauses: A product key for a different edition (Home vs Pro)
A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

prevention: Link your digital license to your Microsoft account
Buy keys from Microsoft or authorized sellers
Keep a record of the product key and where it came from

title: Error 0xC00B0001
summary: 0xC00B0001 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_MUI_FILE_NOT_FOUND The resource loader failed to find an MUI file"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC00B0001 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0130006
summary: 0xC0130006 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0130006 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC013000A
summary: 0xC013000A is a Windows system error: "STATUS_CLUSTER_INVALID_REQUEST The cluster request is not valid for this object". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC013000A is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_CLUSTER_INVALID_REQUEST The cluster request is not valid for this object". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0150005
summary: 0xC0150005 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_SXS_MANIFEST_FORMAT_ERROR The manifest file does not begin with the required tag and format information"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.

Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC

fixes.title: Check the current license state

title: Error 0xC0150015
summary: 0xC0150015 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_SXS_CORRUPTION The application isolation metadata for this process or thread has become corrupt"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0150015 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC015001A
summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0xC015001A and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC015001A comes from the Microsoft Store or the app installer service. It means the Store could not download, license or install an app package. The cause is usually local: a stale Store cache, the wrong date and time, a sign-in problem or a stopped service.
commonCauses: A corrupted Microsoft Store cache
Incorrect date, time or region settings
A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

meaning: Error 0xC0150027 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0190001
summary: 0xC0190001 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_TRANSACTIONAL_CONFLICT The function attempted to use a name that is reserved for use by another transaction". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC0190001 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_TRANSACTIONAL_CONFLICT The function attempted to use a name that is reserved for use by another transaction". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0190021
summary: 0xC0190021 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_OBJECT_NO_LONGER_EXISTS The object (file, stream, or link) that corresponds to the handle has been deleted by a transaction savepoint rollback"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0190021 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0xC019004A and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC019004A comes from the Microsoft Store or the app installer service. It means the Store could not download, license or install an app package. The cause is usually local: a stale Store cache, the wrong date and time, a sign-in problem or a stopped service.
commonCauses: A corrupted Microsoft Store cache
Incorrect date, time or region settings
A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep the clock synced automatically
Install Windows updates, since they include Store framework fixes
Avoid blocking Microsoft endpoints in firewall or hosts files

title: Error 0xC0190053
summary: 0xC0190053 appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: Error 0xC0190053 appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

summary: 0xC0190056 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_COMPRESSION_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_TRANSACTION The compression operation could not be completed because a transaction is active on the file"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0190056 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0190058
summary: 0xC0190058 appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: Error 0xC0190058 appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

meaning: Error 0xC01A0005 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_LOG_INVALID_RANGE The log service encountered an attempt to access data outside the active log range". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC01A000D
summary: 0xC01A000D means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_LOG_METADATA_CORRUPT The log service encountered a corrupted metadata file"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC01A000D relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app

title: Error 0xC01C0007
summary: 0xC01C0007 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC01C0007 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC01C0017
summary: 0xC01C0017 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC01C0017 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC01C0018
summary: 0xC01C0018 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_FLT_NAME_CACHE_MISS The name requested was not found in the Filter Manager name cache and could not be retrieved from the file system"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC01C0018 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors

title: Error 0xC01D0006
summary: 0xC01D0006 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_MONITOR_INVALID_SERIAL_NUMBER_MONDSC_BLOCK The provided monitor descriptor block is either corrupted or does not contain the monitor's detailed serial number"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC01D0006 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC01E0001
summary: 0xC01E0001 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0001 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC01E0004
summary: 0xC01E0004 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0004 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

fixes.title: Trim startup apps

fixes.title: Scan for malware

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

title: Error 0xC01E0200
summary: 0xC01E0200 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0200 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC01E0347
summary: 0xC01E0347 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0347 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

Back up regularly to more than one place

Outdated drivers
