fixes.title: Trim startup apps
fixes.detail: Task Manager > Startup apps: disable anything you do not need at sign-in.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates

title: Error 0xC01E0438
summary: 0xC01E0438 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0438 is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC01E0503
summary: 0xC01E0503 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0503 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC01E0518
summary: 0xC01E0518 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC01E0518 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

fixes.title: Scan for malware

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates

title: Error 0xC01E051E
summary: 0xC01E051E means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC01E051E is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Error 0xC01E058B
summary: 0xC01E058B means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_GRAPHICS_DDCCI_INVALID_MESSAGE_CHECKSUM This error occurred because the value in a DDC/CI message's checksum field did not match the message's computed checksum value. This error implies that the data was corrupted while it was being transmitted from a monitor to a computer"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC01E058B relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive

fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

title: Error 0xC0210004
summary: 0xC0210004 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_FVE_FAILED_WRONG_FS The partition cannot be encrypted because the file system is not supported"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC0210004 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0210008
summary: Windows activation failed with 0xC0210008. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.
meaning: Error 0xC0210008 is an activation result. Windows could not confirm that this PC has a valid license, either because the key does not match the installed edition, the license is tied to different hardware, or the activation servers could not be reached.
commonCauses: A product key for a different edition (Home vs Pro)
A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

prevention: Link your digital license to your Microsoft account
Buy keys from Microsoft or authorized sellers
Keep a record of the product key and where it came from

summary: Windows Update reported 0xC021000F ("STATUS_FVE_OVERLAPPED_UPDATE The control block for the encrypted volume was updated by another thread. Try again") and the update could not finish. Clearing the update cache and repairing system components fixes most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC021000F is a result code returned while Windows Update was downloading, preparing or installing an update. Its underlying message is: "STATUS_FVE_OVERLAPPED_UPDATE The control block for the encrypted volume was updated by another thread. Try again". The update itself is rarely broken; the usual problem is on the PC: a corrupted download cache, stopped update services, too little free space, damaged system components or something blocking the connection to Microsoft's servers.
commonCauses: A corrupted or half-finished download in the SoftwareDistribution cache
Windows Update, BITS or Cryptographic services stopped or disabled
Too little free space on the system drive
Corrupted component store or system files
A VPN, proxy, firewall or third-party antivirus interfering with the download

fixes.title: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters and click Run next to Windows Update. On Windows 10 it is under Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot. Restart and try again.

fixes.title: Free up disk space
fixes.detail: Make sure the system drive has at least 20 GB free. Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files lets you remove old update files and other clutter safely.

fixes.title: Reset the update download cache
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `net stop wuauserv`, `net stop bits` and `net stop cryptsvc`. Rename the cache with `ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old`, then start the services again with `net start cryptsvc`, `net start bits` and `net start wuauserv`.
fixes.riskNote: Renaming the folder clears your local update history view. Installed updates are not affected.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Install the update manually
fixes.detail: Note the KB number shown in Settings > Windows Update, search for it in the Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com), download the package for your Windows version and architecture, and run it.

fixes.title: Run an in-place repair install as a last resort
fixes.detail: Download the Windows installation media from Microsoft, run setup.exe from inside Windows and choose to keep personal files and apps. It replaces every system file without wiping your data.
fixes.riskNote: Back up your important files before starting, and keep the PC plugged in until setup completes.

prevention: Keep at least 20 GB free on the system drive
Do not shut down while "Working on updates" is on screen
Pause VPNs and third-party firewalls while large updates download
Run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth` now and then to catch component damage early

title: Error 0xC0210010
summary: 0xC0210010 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_FVE_FAILED_SECTOR_SIZE The volume encryption algorithm cannot be used on this sector size". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC0210010 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_FVE_FAILED_SECTOR_SIZE The volume encryption algorithm cannot be used on this sector size". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0210011
summary: 0xC0210011 appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: Error 0xC0210011 appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

title: Error 0xC021001D
summary: The Microsoft Store returned 0xC021001D and could not finish downloading or installing an app. A cache reset, a clock check and a fresh sign-in solve most cases.
meaning: Error 0xC021001D comes from the Microsoft Store or the app installer service. It means the Store could not download, license or install an app package. The cause is usually local: a stale Store cache, the wrong date and time, a sign-in problem or a stopped service.

Incorrect date, time or region settings
A problem with the Microsoft account sign-in or license
Store-related services stopped or disabled
A proxy or VPN blocking Store traffic

fixes.title: Reset the Store cache
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `wsreset.exe` and press Enter. A blank window opens for a few seconds and the Store relaunches with a fresh cache.

fixes.title: Check date, time and region
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Time & language and turn on "Set time automatically" and "Set time zone automatically", then click Sync now. Make sure Region matches where you are.

fixes.title: Sign out of the Store and back in
fixes.detail: Open the Store, click your profile picture, sign out, restart the PC and sign in again with the same Microsoft account.

fixes.title: Run the Windows Store Apps troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Store Apps > Run.

fixes.title: Repair or reset the Store app
fixes.detail: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Store > Advanced options. Try Repair first, then Reset if the problem remains.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep the clock synced automatically
Install Windows updates, since they include Store framework fixes
Avoid blocking Microsoft endpoints in firewall or hosts files

title: Error 0xC021001E

title: Error 0xC021001F

Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version

Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC0210026
summary: Windows activation failed with 0xC0210026. The license, the product key and the edition need to line up, and the steps below check each one.
meaning: Error 0xC0210026 is an activation result. Windows could not confirm that this PC has a valid license, either because the key does not match the installed edition, the license is tied to different hardware, or the activation servers could not be reached.
commonCauses: A product key for a different edition (Home vs Pro)
A major hardware change, especially a new motherboard
A volume license or KMS key on a home PC
No internet connection or a blocked connection to the activation servers
The key was already used on more PCs than its license allows

fixes.title: Check the current license state
fixes.detail: Open Settings > System > Activation to read the status message. For detail, run `slmgr /dlv` in an elevated prompt: it shows the edition, the license channel and the partial key.

fixes.title: Run the Activation troubleshooter
fixes.detail: On the Activation page click Troubleshoot. If you recently changed hardware and your license is linked to your Microsoft account, choose "I changed hardware on this device recently".

fixes.title: Enter the correct product key
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Activation > Change product key. Use the key that matches the installed edition. Keys from a different edition will not activate.

fixes.title: Retry online activation from the command line
fixes.detail: Run `slmgr /ato` in an elevated prompt while connected to the internet. Disable VPNs or proxies first.

prevention: Link your digital license to your Microsoft account
Buy keys from Microsoft or authorized sellers
Keep a record of the product key and where it came from

title: Error 0xC0220002
summary: 0xC0220002 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_FWP_CONDITION_NOT_FOUND The filter condition does not exist". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC0220002 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_FWP_CONDITION_NOT_FOUND The filter condition does not exist". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

title: Error 0xC0220013
summary: 0xC0220013 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0220013 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC0220018
summary: 0xC0220018 appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: Error 0xC0220018 appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading.
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

title: Error 0xC022001A
summary: 0xC022001A means Windows or Microsoft Defender blocked an action ("STATUS_FWP_TRAFFIC_MISMATCH The traffic parameters do not match those for the security association context"). The steps below separate a deliberate block from a broken setting.
meaning: Error 0xC022001A is a security or permissions result: Windows, Microsoft Defender or a policy refused an action. Sometimes that is exactly the right outcome (a blocked threat); other times a setting, a leftover security product or damaged permissions is blocking something legitimate.
commonCauses: Insufficient permissions for the account or process
A third-party security product, or its leftovers after removal
Group Policy or registry settings restricting the feature
Corrupted Defender or Windows Security components
Malware tampering with security settings

fixes.title: Retry with administrator rights
fixes.detail: Run the program or command as administrator. In a work or school PC, ask your IT team, since policies may block the action deliberately.

fixes.title: Check Windows Security status
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security and review Virus & threat protection and Protection history. Restore or allow items only if you are sure they are safe.

fixes.title: Remove leftover security software
fixes.detail: Uninstall any old antivirus from Settings > Apps, then use the vendor's removal tool to clear leftovers.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Run one antivirus product at a time
Use a standard account for daily work
Keep Windows Security definitions up to date

title: Error 0xC022001C
summary: 0xC022001C is a Windows system error: "STATUS_FWP_NULL_POINTER A required pointer is null". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC022001C is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_FWP_NULL_POINTER A required pointer is null". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC022001E
summary: 0xC022001E slows the PC down. Find the process responsible in Task Manager, then work through the fixes below.
meaning: Error 0xC022001E is a performance problem rather than a crash: something is using more CPU, disk, memory or time than it should. Finding the process responsible is usually the whole battle.
commonCauses: Too many apps launching at startup
A background update, indexing or antivirus scan
Malware or unwanted software
A nearly full or failing drive
Outdated drivers

fixes.title: Find the process using the resources
fixes.detail: Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc), go to Processes and sort by CPU, Memory or Disk. Note the top process before changing anything.

fixes.title: Trim startup apps
fixes.detail: Task Manager > Startup apps: disable anything you do not need at sign-in.

fixes.title: Scan for malware
fixes.detail: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options and run a Full scan. If something keeps coming back, run Microsoft Defender Offline scan from the same page.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

prevention: Keep 15-20% of the system drive free
Uninstall software you no longer use
Avoid running multiple antivirus products

title: Error 0xC022001F
summary: 0xC022001F means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC022001F is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

meaning: Error 0xC0220033 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_FWP_NEVER_MATCH The enumeration template or subscription will never match any objects". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Try a clean boot to rule out background software
fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

prevention: Install software from the vendor rather than bundles or mirrors
Keep Windows and your apps updated
Avoid "registry cleaner" and "PC optimizer" tools
Create a restore point before large installs

title: Error 0xC0220035
summary: 0xC0220035 points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC0220035 points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

title: Error 0xC0220100
summary: 0xC0220100 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0220100 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC0230015
summary: 0xC0230015 is a Windows system error: "STATUS_NDIS_INVALID_DATA The data used for this operation is not valid". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Error 0xC0230015 is a Windows system error code with the official message "STATUS_NDIS_INVALID_DATA The data used for this operation is not valid". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. The surrounding context (which app, which file, which action) tells you what actually failed.
commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

title: Error 0xC0230017
summary: 0xC0230017 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC0230017 is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC023001B
summary: 0xC023001B means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_NDIS_FILE_NOT_FOUND An attempt was made to map a file that cannot be found"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC023001B relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Error 0xC023001E
summary: 0xC023001E points at a hardware fault. Back up first, then test memory, storage and temperatures in that order.
meaning: Error 0xC023001E points at the physical side of the PC: memory, storage, the processor, graphics or power delivery reported a fault that software could not hide. Hardware errors often start rare and become more frequent, so it is worth testing now rather than waiting.
commonCauses: Failing or incompatible RAM
A storage drive with bad sectors or a failing controller
Overheating from dust, dried thermal paste or blocked airflow
An unstable overclock, undervolt or XMP/EXPO profile
A weak or aging power supply

fixes.title: Back up your important files now
fixes.detail: Before testing, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage. If hardware is failing, every extra hour of use is a risk.

fixes.title: Return to stock settings
fixes.detail: Disable overclocking and XMP/EXPO memory profiles in UEFI/BIOS (or load optimized defaults), then test whether the problem continues.

fixes.title: Test the memory
fixes.detail: Run `mdsched.exe` and choose "Restart now and check for problems". Any reported error means a RAM stick (or its settings) needs attention. For a deeper test, run MemTest86 from a USB stick for several passes.
fixes.riskNote: The test runs outside Windows, so plan for the PC to be unavailable while it works.

fixes.title: Check the drive health
fixes.detail: In Terminal (Admin) run `wmic diskdrive get model,status` or, in PowerShell, `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter`. The drive maker's tool gives the full SMART report.

fixes.title: Check temperatures and cooling
fixes.detail: Watch CPU and GPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool. Clean dust out of fans and heatsinks, and make sure vents are not blocked.

prevention: Keep the PC clean and well ventilated
Use a quality power supply with headroom for your parts
Back up regularly to more than one place

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

fixes.title: Repair or reinstall the program
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find the program, open its menu and choose Modify, Repair or Advanced options > Repair if offered. Otherwise uninstall it, restart and install the latest version from the vendor.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC

fixes.detail: Run `msconfig`, on the Services tab tick "Hide all Microsoft services" and click "Disable all", then disable startup apps in Task Manager and restart. If the error disappears, re-enable items in small groups to find the one responsible.

title: Error 0xC023002D
summary: 0xC023002D means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Error 0xC023002D is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Error 0xC03A0014
summary: 0xC03A0014 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("STATUS_VIRTDISK_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND A virtual disk support provider for the specified file was not found"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Error 0xC03A0014 relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Win32 error 1641 (0x80070669)
summary: 0x80070669 appears during startup and prevents Windows from loading normally. The recovery environment has the tools to repair it.
meaning: Win32 error 1641 (0x80070669) appears while Windows is starting. Something in the boot chain (firmware settings, the boot configuration data, the system drive or an early-loading driver) is missing or damaged, so Windows cannot finish loading. Technically, 0x80070669 is an HRESULT that wraps Win32 error 1641 (ERROR_SUCCESS_REBOOT_INITIATED).
commonCauses: Damaged boot configuration data (BCD) or boot files
A changed storage mode (AHCI/RAID) or boot order in UEFI/BIOS
A failed update or driver installed just before the restart
A failing or disconnected system drive
Power loss during an update

fixes.title: Disconnect extra drives and devices
fixes.detail: Unplug USB drives, card readers, docks and other non-essential devices, then restart. A wrong boot device order is a common and harmless cause.

fixes.title: Run Startup Repair
fixes.detail: Interrupt startup three times in a row or boot from Windows installation media, then choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair.

fixes.title: Uninstall the latest update from recovery
fixes.detail: In Advanced options choose Uninstall Updates, then remove the latest quality update first. Try the feature update only if that does not help.

fixes.title: Check the disk from the recovery prompt
fixes.detail: In Advanced options > Command Prompt, run `chkdsk C: /f` (use `bcdedit` or `diskpart` > `list volume` to confirm the Windows drive letter first).

fixes.title: Rebuild the boot configuration
fixes.detail: From the recovery Command Prompt run `bootrec /scanos` and `bootrec /rebuildbcd`. On UEFI systems, `bcdboot C:\Windows` recreates the boot files.
fixes.riskNote: Editing boot records can make things worse if the wrong drive is targeted. Back up data first if you can reach it from another PC.

prevention: Never power off while Windows shows update progress
Do not change SATA or RAID mode in firmware after Windows is installed
Keep a Windows recovery USB drive ready
Back up regularly to an external or cloud location

title: Win32 error 2102 (0x80070836)
summary: 0x80070836 means Windows could not start or use a device properly. Reconnecting the device and repairing its driver fixes most cases.
meaning: Win32 error 2102 (0x80070836) is a device or driver problem reported by Device Manager or the driver framework. Windows found the device but could not start it, load its driver, or keep it running, so the hardware is unavailable until the driver situation is fixed.
commonCauses: A missing, corrupted or incompatible driver
A driver update that introduced a bug
A device that is disconnected, underpowered or failing
Conflicting leftover drivers from older hardware
Firmware or BIOS that needs an update

fixes.title: Read the full device status
fixes.detail: Open Device Manager (`devmgmt.msc`), double-click the device with the warning icon and read "Device status" on the General tab. Note the code number shown there.

fixes.title: Reconnect or power-cycle the device
fixes.detail: Unplug USB devices and plug them into a different port (preferably directly on the PC). For internal hardware, shut down fully and hold the power button for 30 seconds before starting again.

fixes.title: Roll back or update the driver
fixes.detail: In the device properties open the Driver tab. Use Roll Back Driver if the problem started after an update, otherwise install the newest driver from the device or PC maker.

fixes.title: Uninstall the device and let Windows reinstall it
fixes.detail: Right-click the device > Uninstall device (tick "Attempt to remove the driver" if offered), then restart. Windows detects the device again and installs a fresh driver.

fixes.title: Install pending Windows and driver updates
fixes.detail: Open Settings > Windows Update, install everything offered (including optional driver updates), then restart. Many known faults are fixed by a cumulative update or a newer vendor driver.

prevention: Get drivers from the hardware maker or Windows Update
Create a restore point before installing new drivers
Avoid unpowered USB hubs for demanding devices

title: Win32 error 2103 (0x80070837)
summary: 0x80070837 is a Windows system error: "NERR_UnknownServer The server could not be located". The program or feature that showed it tells you where to start, and the fixes below cover the common causes.
meaning: Win32 error 2103 (0x80070837) is a Windows system error code with the official message "NERR_UnknownServer The server could not be located". Programs, installers and Windows features pass these codes up when a lower-level operation fails, so the same number can appear in very different places. commonCauses: A missing, locked or damaged file that the program needs
Insufficient permissions for the folder, registry key or service involved
Security software blocking the operation
Corrupted system files or a broken program install
A setting changed by a recent update or another program

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Run the action again as administrator
fixes.detail: Right-click the program or installer and choose "Run as administrator". If that works, the failure was a permissions problem rather than a broken file.

fixes.title: Look up the event in Event Viewer
fixes.detail: Press Win + R, type `eventvwr.msc`, then open Windows Logs > System (or Application). Filter by the time of the failure and read the Error entries around it: the Source and Event ID usually name the component involved.

title: Win32 error 2104 (0x80070838)
summary: 0x80070838 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Win32 error 2104 (0x80070838) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Win32 error 2131 (0x80070853)
summary: 0x80070853 means Windows could not read, write or access a file or folder ("NERR_LanmanIniError An error occurred when opening or reading the configuration file"). Permissions, file locks and disk errors are the usual suspects.
meaning: Win32 error 2131 (0x80070853) relates to files, folders or the file system. Windows could not read, write, move or trust some data on disk, either because of permissions, a lock held by another process, or damage to the file system itself.
commonCauses: File system damage after a power cut or forced shutdown
Bad sectors on a failing drive
Permissions or ownership that block access
Another process holding the file open
Security software quarantining or locking the file

fixes.title: Restart once and note what you see
fixes.detail: Do a full restart (Start > Power > Restart, not Shut down, because Fast Startup keeps parts of the old session). If the error returns, write down the exact code, the time and what you were doing. Those three details make every later step faster.

fixes.title: Check permissions and ownership
fixes.detail: Right-click the file or folder > Properties > Security. Confirm your account has the access it needs. Only take ownership of your own data folders, never system folders.

fixes.title: Check the disk for file system errors
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `chkdsk C: /scan`. If it reports problems, schedule a repair with `chkdsk C: /f` and restart so it can run before Windows loads.
fixes.riskNote: A full repair pass on a large or failing drive can take a long time. Back up important files first and do not power off while it runs.

fixes.title: Repair system files with DISM and SFC
fixes.detail: Open Terminal (Admin) and run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth` first, then `sfc /scannow`. Let both finish without interrupting, then restart.

fixes.title: Restore from a backup or previous version
fixes.detail: Right-click the folder > Properties > Previous Versions (if File History or restore points exist), or restore the file from your backup.

prevention: Use safely remove for external drives
Keep backups with File History or OneDrive
Watch drive health and replace drives that report errors

title: Win32 error 2136 (0x80070858)
summary: 0x80070858 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Win32 error 2136 (0x80070858) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated

title: Win32 error 2144 (0x80070860)
summary: 0x80070860 means Windows or an app could not complete a network operation. Work from the router to the adapter driver to find where the connection breaks.
meaning: Win32 error 2144 (0x80070860) is a networking error: Windows or an app could not reach a network resource. The fault can sit anywhere along the path, from the adapter driver and its settings, through DNS and the router, to the remote service itself.
commonCauses: An outdated or misbehaving network adapter driver
Corrupted TCP/IP or Winsock settings
DNS problems or a stale DNS cache
VPN, proxy or firewall software intercepting traffic
A router or ISP problem

fixes.title: Restart the router and the PC
fixes.detail: Unplug the router (and modem) for 30 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it is fully online, then restart the PC.

fixes.title: Run the Network troubleshooter
fixes.detail: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Network and Internet > Run.

fixes.title: Flush DNS and renew the address
fixes.detail: In an elevated prompt run `ipconfig /flushdns`, then `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew`.

fixes.title: Reset Winsock and TCP/IP
fixes.detail: Run `netsh winsock reset` and `netsh int ip reset` in an elevated prompt, then restart.

fixes.title: Update or reinstall the network driver
fixes.detail: Device Manager > Network adapters > your adapter > Update driver, or download the latest driver from the PC or adapter maker. Uninstalling the device and restarting makes Windows reinstall it cleanly.

fixes.title: Use Network reset
fixes.detail: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. It reinstalls every adapter and returns network settings to defaults.
fixes.riskNote: Saved Wi-Fi passwords and VPN adapters are removed, so have them ready.

prevention: Keep network drivers current from the hardware maker
Remove VPN clients you no longer use
Restart the router occasionally and keep its firmware updated
